cards.text: Paul the apostle is wrapping up his letter to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's afraid that when he comes, he'll find quarreling and people who sinned and haven't repented (2 Corinthians 12:20-21), and he tells them, "This is the third time I am coming to you." Friend, NOBODY has ever announced a third time in a happy voice.

cards.question: Before he comes, Paul quotes a rule for settling things (Deuteronomy 19:15). The rule says one witness is enough to settle a matter. True or false?

cards.text: Paul already warned them on his second visit, and now, while he's away, he warns them again. Friend, that's a reminder written in ALL CAPS.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians that if he comes back, he'll go easy on everyone except the ones who sinned earlier. True or false?
Paul won't spare anyone, because the Corinthians are demanding proof about him. Proof of what?

answers.text: That Christ is speaking through Paul
That Paul learned from Peter in Jerusalem
That Paul was trained under Gamaliel

cards.text: Paul says Christ is not weak in dealing with them but is powerful among them. Then he points them to the cross.

cards.question: Paul says Christ was crucified in ___, yet He lives by God's ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "For we are also weak in Him, yet by God's power we will live with Him concerning you." Weak doesn't mean finished, friend, because I looked finished for YEARS in a junk drawer, and now LOOK at this mustache!

cards.question: The Corinthians demanded proof from Paul. Now Paul tells them to examine and test themselves. What are they checking?

answers.text: Whether they are in the faith

cards.text: Paul asks if they realize that Jesus Christ is in them, unless they fail the test. Then he says, "And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test."

cards.question: Paul and those with him pray to God that the Corinthians will do what is right. It's not so Paul's group will look like it passed the test. Paul wants the Corinthians to do right even if what happens?

answers.text: Paul's group appears to have failed
Paul's group never hears about it
Paul's group never gets to visit

cards.question: Paul writes, "For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth." He goes on: Paul's group rejoices when they are weak but the Corinthians are ___.

cards.text: Paul's prayer is for their perfection, and he says this is why he writes while he's away: so he won't need to be severe when he's there. It's the oven timer beeping BEFORE the cookies burn, friend.

cards.question: Paul says the Lord gave him authority. What did the Lord give it to him for?

answers.text: To collect the gift for Jerusalem

cards.text: Then Paul starts his goodbye: "Finally, brothers, rejoice!" All those warnings, and he lands on REJOICE, like a friend who tells you the hard truth and then hugs you before you can even get mad.

cards.question: After telling the Corinthians to rejoice, Paul gives them a short list for living together: encourage one another, be of one mind, and more. What else is on it?

answers.text: Aim for perfect harmony and live in peace
Keep away from anyone who sinned before
Stay quiet and wait until Paul arrives

cards.question: After his list for living together, Paul tells the Corinthians that the God of love and peace will be with them. True or false?

cards.text: Paul tells them to greet one another with a holy kiss. And all the saints send their greetings.

cards.question: Paul's last line names the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God. What else does it name?

answers.text: The fellowship of the Holy Spirit

cards.question: After all his warnings, Paul's last line is only for the Corinthians who have repented. True or false?
